first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and has two inherited signals of improved early activation. I would verify memory_86 for durability and qualified-revenue effects, while verifying memory_73 to assess whether promotional pricing produced lasting qualified revenue versus discount-driven acquisition. Pricing may answer the competitor threat, but its margin, retention, and customer-quality risks make it less clearly aligned with sustainable long-term revenue until verified.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable value rather than only top-of-funnel lift. Promotional pricing is rejected despite qualified-revenue growth because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort did not survive first renewal. Longer-term qualified revenue beyond 30 days remains unproven, so the change should remain experimental rather than broadly rolled out.
